The invention relates to an elongated pelt board intended for receiving and supporting an animal pelt during processing, drying, or storage. The pelt board is generally shaped to extend in a longitudinal direction and is configured to fit inside the pelt so that the pelt may be stretched and held in a desired form.

The pelt board comprises four wall elements arranged around the longitudinal axis of the board. These wall elements are positioned in two spaced pairs along two different radial directions. In this way, the wall elements together form an outer support structure for the pelt while also defining an internal cavity that extends along the longitudinal direction of the board.

The wall elements are movable relative to one another. More specifically, they can be displaced between a contracted state and an expanded state. In the contracted state, the radial distances between opposing or corresponding wall elements are reduced, allowing the pelt board to have a smaller overall cross-sectional size. This may facilitate insertion of the board into a pelt or removal of the board after use. In the expanded state, the radial distances between the wall elements are increased, thereby enlarging the effective cross-section of the pelt board and enabling the pelt to be stretched or supported more firmly.

To control this movement, the pelt board further comprises an elongated core element arranged within the cavity defined by the wall elements. The core element is configured to move in the longitudinal direction relative to the wall elements. By longitudinal displacement of the core element, the wall elements are urged between the contracted and expanded states. Thus, the core element functions as an actuator or expansion member, allowing the pelt board to be selectively adjusted between a smaller insertion or removal configuration and a larger pelt-supporting configuration.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to an elongated pelt board intended for receiving and holding an animal pelt during drying, storage, handling, or other treatment. The pelt board has a longitudinal direction and is formed with four elongated wall elements which are arranged at a distance from one another around a central longitudinal cavity. Together, the wall elements define an outer supporting surface for the pelt and an inner space extending along at least a substantial part of the length of the board. The wall elements are movable relative to one another so that the pelt board can assume at least a contracted state and an expanded state.

In the contracted state, the wall elements are positioned closer together, giving the pelt board a reduced transverse dimension. This makes it easier to insert the board into a pelt, particularly where the pelt opening is narrow or where the pelt is delicate and must not be overstretched during mounting. In the expanded state, the wall elements are displaced outwardly from the longitudinal cavity, thereby increasing the circumference or transverse size of the board. When expanded, the board more effectively tensions and supports the pelt from the inside, promoting a desired shape and improved drying conditions.

The adjustment of the wall elements is controlled by an elongated core element arranged within the longitudinal cavity. The core element is movable in the longitudinal direction of the pelt board and cooperates with the wall elements, either directly or through guide surfaces, wedge portions, link elements, or similar mechanical engagement means. When the core element is displaced in one longitudinal direction, the cooperation between the core element and the wall elements causes the wall elements to move outwardly into the expanded state. When the core element is displaced in the opposite longitudinal direction, the wall elements are permitted or forced to move inwardly toward the contracted state.

This construction provides a pelt board which can be adjusted in a controlled and repeatable manner. The user may first place the pelt board in its contracted state, insert it into the animal pelt, and thereafter move the core element so that the board expands to a selected size. The expansion can be gradual, allowing the pelt to be stretched evenly and reducing the risk of tearing, deformation, or uneven tensioning. After drying or treatment, the core element may be moved back to contract the board, making removal of the pelt easier and reducing friction between the pelt and the board.

The use of four spaced wall elements also provides advantages in terms of stability, ventilation, and shape control. Because the wall elements are separated by gaps and surround the longitudinal cavity, air may circulate more effectively around and through the board structure. This can assist in drying the pelt and may reduce drying time. At the same time, the four wall elements provide sufficient support around the inner side of the pelt to maintain a desired elongated shape.

The pelt board may be made from wood, plastics, composite material, metal, or a combination of such materials. The wall elements may be resiliently biased toward either the contracted or expanded state, or they may be guided mechanically by the core element without separate biasing means. The core element may include tapered portions, wedge faces, cam surfaces, or other profiles that convert longitudinal movement of the core into transverse movement of the wall elements. A locking or retaining mechanism may also be provided to hold the core element in a selected position, thereby maintaining the board at a desired degree of expansion during use.

In this manner, the invention provides an adjustable pelt board which is simple to operate, accommodates pelts of different sizes, improves insertion and removal, and enables controlled stretching and support of the pelt. The longitudinally movable core element offers a reliable mechanism for changing the effective size of the board, while the four movable wall elements provide a stable and well-distributed supporting structure for the pelt.

**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** may seem small and simple, but it is one of the most important words in the English language. It is called a definite article, and its main purpose is to point to something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener both know about.

“The” helps make communication clear. It can refer to something already mentioned, something unique, or something understood from context. We say “the sun” because there is only one sun in our sky. We say “the teacher” when everyone knows which teacher we mean. Without “the,” many sentences would feel vague or incomplete.

Although it is only three letters long, “the” appears constantly in English writing and speech. It connects ideas, gives detail, and helps organize meaning. This tiny word shows that even the simplest parts of language can have great importance.

counterfactuals.output:
**Formal Patent-Style Description**

An elongated pelt board for supporting and drying an animal pelt, the pelt board comprising an elongated body extending along a longitudinal axis and having a plurality of wall elements arranged about the longitudinal axis. The wall elements are spaced from one another in radial directions relative to the longitudinal axis and define an outer pelt-supporting surface configured to receive and support the pelt.

The pelt board further comprises an elongated core member disposed at least partially within the elongated body and extending generally along the longitudinal axis. The elongated core member is movable relative to the plurality of wall elements between at least a first position and a second position. Movement of the elongated core member changes radial spacing between at least two of the wall elements, thereby altering an effective transverse dimension of the pelt board.

In one embodiment, the elongated core member is configured to urge the wall elements radially outwardly when moved in a first longitudinal direction and to permit the wall elements to move radially inwardly when moved in an opposite longitudinal direction. The wall elements may be resiliently biased toward a reduced-diameter configuration, and the elongated core member may include one or more tapered, wedge-shaped, camming, or expanding portions configured to engage inner surfaces of the wall elements.

The pelt board may thereby be adjustable between an expanded condition for stretching or supporting a pelt and a contracted condition for facilitating insertion into or removal from the pelt.

---

**Example Independent Claim**

1. An elongated pelt board for an animal pelt, comprising:  
   an elongated body extending along a longitudinal axis;  
   a plurality of elongated wall elements extending generally along the longitudinal axis and arranged around the longitudinal axis, the plurality of wall elements defining an outer pelt-supporting surface; and  
   an elongated core member positioned at least partially within the elongated body and movable relative to the plurality of elongated wall elements;  
   wherein movement of the elongated core member changes radial distances between the plurality of elongated wall elements so as to adjust a transverse size of the elongated pelt board.

---

**Example Dependent Claims**

2. The elongated pelt board of claim 1, wherein the elongated core member is movable longitudinally relative to the plurality of elongated wall elements.

3. The elongated pelt board of claim 1, wherein the elongated core member comprises at least one tapered portion configured to engage inner surfaces of the plurality of elongated wall elements.

4. The elongated pelt board of claim 3, wherein longitudinal displacement of the elongated core member causes the at least one tapered portion to urge the plurality of elongated wall elements radially outwardly.

5. The elongated pelt board of claim 1, wherein the plurality of elongated wall elements are movable between a contracted configuration and an expanded configuration.

6. The elongated pelt board of claim 5, wherein the contracted configuration facilitates removal of the pelt board from the animal pelt.

7. The elongated pelt board of claim 5, wherein the expanded configuration tensions the animal pelt on the outer pelt-supporting surface.

8. The elongated pelt board of claim 1, wherein the plurality of elongated wall elements are circumferentially spaced about the longitudinal axis.

9. The elongated pelt board of claim 1, further comprising at least one biasing member configured to bias at least one of the plurality of elongated wall elements radially inwardly.

10. The elongated pelt board of claim 1, wherein the elongated core member is removable from the elongated body.

11. The elongated pelt board of claim 1, wherein the elongated core member includes a plurality of cam surfaces positioned to engage corresponding inner surfaces of the plurality of elongated wall elements.

12. The elongated pelt board of claim 1, wherein the plurality of elongated wall elements collectively define a generally tapered outer profile along the longitudinal axis.

13. The elongated pelt board of claim 1, wherein the elongated body has a first end and a second end, and wherein the elongated core member is actuatable from at least one of the first end or the second end.

14. The elongated pelt board of claim 1, wherein the wall elements comprise wood, polymer, metal, composite material, or combinations thereof.

15. The elongated pelt board of claim 1, wherein movement of the elongated core member changes an effective width of the pelt board while maintaining the wall elements in a generally longitudinal orientation.

---

**Example Method Claim**

16. A method of supporting an animal pelt on an elongated pelt board, comprising:  
   positioning an animal pelt over an elongated body having a plurality of elongated wall elements arranged about a longitudinal axis;  
   moving an elongated core member relative to the plurality of elongated wall elements; and  
   in response to movement of the elongated core member, changing radial distances between the plurality of elongated wall elements to adjust a transverse size of the elongated pelt board and support the animal pelt.

17. The method of claim 16, further comprising moving the elongated core member to expand the pelt board after the animal pelt is positioned on the elongated body.

18. The method of claim 16, further comprising moving the elongated core member to contract the pelt board before removing the pelt board from the animal pelt.

---

**Example Abstract**

An adjustable elongated pelt board for animal pelts includes a plurality of elongated wall elements arranged around a longitudinal axis to define an outer pelt-supporting surface. An elongated core member is positioned at least partially within the wall elements and is movable relative thereto. Movement of the core member changes radial spacing between the wall elements, thereby adjusting the transverse size of the pelt board. The core member may include tapered or camming surfaces that urge the wall elements outwardly to expand the board, while inward movement or biasing of the wall elements permits contraction to facilitate removal from a pelt.
